findings.evidence: Torus.lean:85-86 `def diagonalTorus ... := MonoidHom.range (diagGL (k := k) (n := n))`; Torus.lean:89-91 `@[simp] theorem mem_diagonalTorus_iff`; Centralizer.lean:132 `= (diagGL (k := F) (n := 2)).range`.
findings.fix: State `Subgroup.centralizer {diagGL t} = diagonalTorus F 2`. `Torus.lean` sits under `RepresentationTheory` (it imports `ClassicalGroups.Standard`), so first move `diagonalTorus`, `mem_diagonalTorus_iff`, `diagonalTorusEquiv` and the centralizer lemmas down to `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Diagonal.lean` (with `isUnit_apply_of_isDiag`), updating all uses and deleting the old location — no forwarding module, per the compatibility policy. The `Nat.card (diagonalTorus k n) = (Nat.card k - 1) ^ n` fact then belongs on the torus, not inside this centralizer file.
findings.issue: `centralizer_diagGL` states the split torus as the raw `(diagGL (k := F) (n := 2)).range`, but that subgroup already has a canonical name: `TauCeti.diagonalTorus k n := MonoidHom.range (diagGL (k := k) (n := n))` (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups/Torus.lean:85-86), with `@[simp] mem_diagonalTorus_iff`, `diagonalTorusEquiv` and `centralizer_diagonalTorus` attached to it. Consumers of the new theorem land on a spelling none of that API matches syntactically, so `mem_diagonalTorus_iff` will not fire and the two split-torus results cannot be combined without unfolding. `natCard_centralizer_diagGL` repeats the problem by recomputing `Nat.card` of that subgroup from `diagGL_injective` rather than from the named torus.

findings.evidence: Commute.lean:67-69 `private theorem scalar_add_smul_apply ... = (if i = j then a else 0) + b * M i j`; Centralizer.lean:138-141 states and proves the same equation for `M := diagGL t`.
findings.fix: Make `scalar_add_smul_apply` public (it is the characteristic entry lemma for the commutant description) and replace the `hentry` block in `centralizer_diagGL` with it.
findings.issue: `scalar_add_smul_apply` — the entrywise reading of the `a • 1 + b • M` normal form that `commute_finTwo_iff` hands out — is `private`, yet its statement is re-proved verbatim by the first consumer: `Centralizer.lean:138-141` establishes `(h : Matrix _ _ F) i j = (if i = j then a else 0) + b * (diagGL t) i j` by `rw [hab]; simp [Matrix.scalar_apply, Matrix.diagonal_apply]`, which after the rewrite is exactly `scalar_add_smul_apply a b i j`. A helper with a demonstrated use outside the file it serves should not be private: every user of `commute_finTwo_iff` has to redo this unfolding by hand.

findings.fix: Generalize to `{M : Type*} [Monoid M] {g h : Mˣ} : h ∈ Subgroup.centralizer {g} ↔ Commute (g : M) (h : M)`, and place it with the group-theory material rather than in the `GL₂` file.
findings.issue: `mem_centralizer_singleton_iff_commute_coe` is exported only for `g h : GL (Fin 2) F` with `[Field F]`, but neither the statement nor the proof uses the size or the field: it is `Subgroup.mem_centralizer_singleton_iff` composed with `Commute.units_val_iff`, valid for units of any monoid. As stated, no `GL n R` consumer can use it and the same coercion transport gets rewritten by hand elsewhere (Torus.lean:149-151).

findings.evidence: NonSplitTorus.lean:181 `natCard_eq : Nat.card (GL2NonSplitTorus F E hE) = Nat.card F ^ 2 - 1` (no `Fintype`); Centralizer.lean:267,272-273 `variable [Fintype F]` and `... = Fintype.card F ^ 2 - 1` proved by `rw [..., natCard_eq, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]`; Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Units/Fintype.lean:40 `Nat.card_units [GroupWithZero α]`.
findings.fix: State both `natCard_centralizer_*` lemmas with `Nat.card F`, matching `GL2NonSplitTorus.natCard_eq`, and drop `[Fintype F]` from `natCard_centralizer_gl2NonSplitTorusHom` (its proof becomes `rw [centralizer_gl2NonSplitTorusHom hE hx, natCard_eq]`). Keep `[Fintype F]` only on the `ncard_carrier_mk_*` counting results, which genuinely need `Matrix.card_GL_field`.
findings.issue: `natCard_centralizer_gl2NonSplitTorusHom` adds `[Fintype F]` purely to restate its own ingredient in `Fintype.card`: the proof is `centralizer_gl2NonSplitTorusHom` then `natCard_eq`, and `GL2NonSplitTorus.natCard_eq` is `Nat.card F ^ 2 - 1` with no finiteness hypothesis (`Nat.card_units` is unconditional). The `GL2NonSplitTorus` namespace now carries two card conventions for the same quantity, so a consumer combining `natCard_eq` and `natCard_centralizer_gl2NonSplitTorusHom` must insert `Nat.card_eq_fintype_card`. Same convention split in `natCard_centralizer_diagGL` (line 166).

summary: The centralizer of a split element is stated against the raw `MonoidHom.range diagGL` although the repo already names that subgroup `TauCeti.diagonalTorus`, giving two public spellings of the same object; a private helper is re-proved verbatim in the consumer file; and one general units lemma is exported only for `GL (Fin 2)` over a field.
